prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1292; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim received by phone from the insured driver of the vehicle struck in the rear at a signalized intersection. Insured reports a sudden stop by the lead vehicle, followed by impact. Driver states she felt immediate neck stiffness and lower back soreness. Vehicle is drivable but has visible rear bumper damage. Recorded statement scheduled.

Entry 2: Recorded statement taken from the claimant. She confirms she was stopped at a red light when the rear impact occurred. Speed at impact estimated as low. No airbag deployment. She was seen at an urgent care clinic the same afternoon and given a diagnosis of cervical and lumbar strain. She has not retained an attorney and says she is handling the claim herself. Advised her of the claims process and that she may request a copy of the police report.

Entry 3: Photos of both vehicles received through the claimant's upload link. Damage to claimant's rear bumper and trunk lid is consistent with the reported impact. Other driver's front bumper shows matching damage. Police report obtained and reviewed; it notes both drivers were cooperative and that the at-fault driver was cited for following too closely. Liability appears clear.

Entry 4: Called claimant for an update. She reports ongoing neck pain rated moderate and stiffness when turning her head. Lower back discomfort has eased somewhat with rest. She has been attending physical therapy twice a week. Provided her with a medical authorization form and explained how to submit treatment records. She asked how bodily injury claims are evaluated; explained that the adjuster will review records once received and that she may submit any out-of-pocket receipts.

Entry 5: Medical records received from the urgent care clinic and physical therapy provider. Records are consistent with the reported neck and back strain and show a treatment plan with a projected recovery timeline. No prior claims or treatment for the same body regions found in the index search. File reviewed with supervisor. Next step is to request updated therapy notes and set a follow-up call with the claimant in two weeks.
